# Test catalog

Question bank backend additions:

- `server/internal/bank/bank_test.go`: independent migration ledger, syllabus/list queries, optimistic saves, review retained on edit, review undo, a purged account's id blanked from the question it edited and reviewed while the question stays (security regression: rate-limit audit r3 N-3, Q350), editor column grants, missing config and unreachable pool.
- `server/internal/cover/cover_test.go`: `Cover.Check` accepts each style's own fields, a seed and the default cover, and refuses an upper-case colour, a missing or stray kind, an unknown pattern, a line outside paper, a bad seed and an unknown style.
- `server/internal/bank/assets_test.go`: immutable content-hash publication metadata and rejection of active, external-resource and oversized SVG assets; `TestRasterFiguresKeepThePixelLimit`: a raster figure past 2,400 px on a side is refused `image_too_large` (security regression: Q348 review N2; fails with the pixel check removed).
- `server/internal/bank/page_test.go`: the topic pager (`PageRows`) pages forward and back by position cursor, `around` lands on the page holding a question, a row that stops matching between pages (answered under the Status filter) shifts nothing, the type, status, search and unreviewed filters, the topic's answer types, and a malformed cursor refused.
- `server/internal/bank/progress_test.go`: the /qb landing's topic progress counts only current answered questions (an edited or retracted question is unanswered, a topic with none is left out), counts full-mark scores as correct, puts the latest answered topic first, and points Continue at the next unanswered question after the latest answer, wrapping to the start, or nowhere once every question is answered.
- `server/internal/httpapi/bank_test.go`: batch reads in request order with attribution and 404 for an unknown id, answer-free single and batch reads for learners and for editors in View mode, the editor-only `/edit` read with the keys (404 for a learner), editor/read-only/suspended gates, stale saves, public SVG upload, library attribution resolved from a retired version's row though its excerpts are gone, with ShareAlike licensing, `CheckExcerpts` refusing that retired excerpt and accepting the current one, web-page attribution and a comment stored as a notice for the digest (none when comments are not configured).
- `scripts/env/test_config.py`: bank owner/private-bucket secrets excluded from the API target and optional bank configuration.

One-line descriptions of every automated test file in the repo (excluding build
artifacts under `collaboration/dist` and vendored packages). Run commands are
at the top of each section.

Responsive styling changes also need a manual viewport check below and above
`sm` (640px): IconPicker uses three/six columns and 350px/440px gallery heights;
SectionGallery spacing and toast action sizing increase at `sm`; workspace
labels, note AI suggestions and editor padding use small-screen base styles.
These visual checks are not covered by the automated suites below.

Chat history styling is checked manually in the MSW Biology workspace: open
Chat history from the right panel's Chat view, inspect the dialog's list (New
chat, search, Pinned and Older, scroll fade) and See archived, select a saved
conversation, reopen to check its active marker, and dismiss with Escape; on a
phone New chat sits in the dialog header and archived rows show icon buttons.

Python checks include a pixels-mode capture landing in production's turn state (its record, pending image and budget image; a cited page's result text equal to production's `_capture_note`; the 16th noting the cap, the 17th refused), description overrides, unchanged argument schemas, live catalog preservation, invalid override rejection, missing model pins returning HTTP errors before streaming, one capture_page schema in previews and live turns, local source-list dispatch without a gateway, forwarding evidence and checkpoints through the turn endpoint (the run recording its library reads), the output preview's deck slides with figures inlined and its `/embed/` frame carrying the CSP line of `embed/_headers`, note fence checks (flashcards, html-embed html without a fallback, size refusals, a CDN script and the SVG namespace accepted, another origin, a lookalike host and `fetch` refused, YAML errors), and the playground-only deck tools (`deck.py`, ppt-master's Quick route; clones the pinned ppt-master into `local/` on first run): the outline returning the style and its reference slides, slides refused for unparseable XML, another canvas, no `lang`, text outside its module (ppt-master's checker), an uncaptured or whole-page figure, or an out-of-range number, an accepted slide with a cropped capture, the `.pptx` exported once every slide is written, and schema validation. The question tools through the run's files: a new quiz saving its valid question and naming the other (a unit with a text answer), the fix (an answer written with its unit), an open question and a plot after the first question's text, each saved quiz passing `quizcheck`, a note's quiz fence expanded from the small shapes with its trailing comma repaired and named, and a later turn adding to the quiz an earlier turn made. Local note writes placing a library figure keep its render under the run's `assets/`, record it on the material for the preview with the printed credit in the caption and the figure's excerpt credited, an edit adds its own, and `add_question_media` places one after a quiz question's text as an image block keeping its `figure:<id>` asset with its render recorded on the quiz. The local `inspect_document`/`read_document`/`edit_document` on a run's note and card set: block ids given once and kept across edits and turns, an insert, block replacement and text replacement landing where their ids say, a stale expected text refusing the call, a card added after another, and a note's Mermaid block inspected as its source, refusing `replace_text` and taking `replace_block` that expects the source exactly (review r2 L3, L4). `library_flow`: `browse_first` leaving browse a subject only, `search_subject` moving the subject list into search and dropping browse. `skill_addons` appended to a skill's text; `preference_text` replacing one preference value's turn-context line for a turn only and refusing a name outside `preferences.py`. |

Playwright's sharing/API global setup builds the collaboration Docker image,
including Office WASM with Binaryen's version and verified archive checksum from
the pinned BetterOffice checkout. On ARM hosts, run
`DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM=linux/amd64 pnpm e2e:slow` for its x86_64 Linux toolchain.

The frontend and browser E2E CI jobs reuse compiled browser WASM through
`.github/actions/cache-betteroffice`; normal `office:prepare` source and output
hash validation still runs before consuming the restored artifacts. This cache
does not cover the separate collaboration Docker build.

`e2e_stack` (WebKit) and `e2e_mermaid_engines` (Firefox and WebKit) install
their browsers through `.github/actions/playwright-browsers`, which keeps the
system packages' `.deb` files in the Actions cache, keyed on the runner image,
the browsers and the Playwright version. The runners' Ubuntu mirror sometimes
serves them at a few KB/s, so an uncached install that slow hits the step's
10-minute timeout; rerun the job.

[`scripts/dev/hosts.test.mjs`](../scripts/dev/hosts.test.mjs) checks macOS/Windows
elevation command construction and argument quoting, hosts paths, idempotent
edits, backup preservation, line endings, aliases and conflicting mappings.

The local grading checks in [`bench/grading/scripts/test_benchmark.py`](../bench/grading/scripts/test_benchmark.py) cover invalid-score handling, family split integrity, interrupted result recovery, separation of run configurations and changed coverage, exclusion of anchors/ambiguous labels from primary matched/native metrics, complete hash-matched comparison with invalid paired scores, and native/browser pairing restricted to identical cases, model hashes and explicit decoding controls. [`test_browser.mjs`](../bench/grading/scripts/test_browser.mjs) checks that a runtime exception saves bounded diagnostic logs, stops requests to the failed worker, releases it, permits the next model to run and visibly reports the failure. Model evaluations are opt-in experiments described in [`bench/grading/README.md`](../bench/grading/README.md), with artifacts under ignored `data/grading-benchmark/`.

[`test_laya_cpu.py`](../bench/grading/scripts/test_laya_cpu.py) checks that partial-award agreement does not hide marking-point errors, and that an inference failure counts as a failure while preserving the archived Jev baseline. `laya_cpu.py prepare` also verifies the archived 1,688-request rubric corpus reproduces Jev's published seed and essay award counts before writing the replay requests.
The opt-in [`alibaba_decision.py`](../bench/grading/scripts/alibaba_decision.py) replay uses the same scoring checks, validates returned question ids and finite probabilities, and records hosted API failures without retries. It requires explicitly selected credentials and an Alibaba workspace endpoint; it is not a CI test.

[`jev_context.py --check`](../bench/grading/scripts/jev_context.py) verifies that the paired 192-call essay comparison removes only question context, preserves inputs and marking definitions, keeps aggregate all/some/none scoring distinct from item-level partial credit, and records failures without converting them to grades. Live runs require an explicit fresh output directory and a Jev credential; they are opt-in benchmarks, not CI tests.

[`jev_partial_credit.py --check`](../bench/grading/scripts/jev_partial_credit.py) checks explicit/plain scheme isolation, paired context, 0.35/0.65 boundaries, malformed/non-finite decision output, failure accounting and exclusion of unknown gold. Its 144-call-per-mode live comparison asks direct three-way and Boolean decisions together; a first-request format/auth gate stops a bad batch without retrying. Synthetic labels and missing-evidence diagnostics are documented in the grading report; this is not a CI test.

[`jev_contract.py --check`](../bench/grading/scripts/jev_contract.py) validates the three production-contract fixtures against the open-part question shape, checks that the four grading arms send identical question objects and differ only in state or packaging, that no gold label or rationale reaches a model payload, that question text matches the app's `blocksToText` assembly, and covers noul bands, score rounding, malformed responses, failure accounting, false-credit counts and computation-check precision/recall. Live runs (`--experiment grading|compute|latex`) need a fresh output directory and a Jev credential; they are opt-in benchmarks, not CI tests.

[`alt_methods.py --check`](../bench/grading/scripts/alt_methods.py) runs the deterministic alternative-method checker (triangle true-quantity table, coordinate circle figure with theorem preconditions, linear solution-set chain) on every fixture answer and checks that no gold label reaches a Jev payload. Live runs need a Jev credential and a fresh output directory; they are opt-in benchmarks, not CI tests.

A `provider_busy` answer is its own retryable kind. A 408 `upload_timeout` (past the gateway's upload deadline) reads as "The upload took too long. On the server's `update-timeout` notice the room pauses (not synced, the tab held back, the notice not passed on, nothing sent: an edit and a checkpoint request meanwhile stay unsent), and when the time is up the same channel joins again on the same socket, its step 2 carrying both edits the server never applied, synced again with one socket throughout and the edits' draft rows kept (Epo 2026-10-18 timeouts; fails with the resume or the pause reverted). An update over 2 MiB goes in ordered pieces of at most 2 MiB that apply with nothing pending, each acknowledged on its own, the tab held back until the last is acknowledged; a resync's step 2 goes in pieces too; past the 8 MiB burst the socket paces pieces under the allowance, held back meanwhile, and a checkpoint request sent after them goes last (Epo 2026-10-18 pieces). A room the server closed as its user's oldest (`collaboration-oldest-closed`, 22 joined documents, Epo 2026-10-19) reports no close and does not join at once, but joins again when the tab shows after being hidden, or on an edit in it; an update holding a piece over the server's 8 MiB cap is never sent: the room closes once and stays stopped through a reconnect (rate-limit review r3 S8, fails with the size check reverted); a parked room ignores an update applied to its document (a restored draft) and joins on a local edit (rate-limit review r4 N-e). The socket an edit token warms (`CollabSocket.warm`) is the one the room then joins on, and one no room joins closes after its 8 s hold and the 5 s idle delay (fails with its behaviour reverted). The server's `open-slowed` notice reaches `onSlowed`, not the stateless handler (Epo 2026-10-20), and a channel closed as the user's oldest while slowed reports the slow over (r6 N-4); a JOIN reserves one message of the tab's allowance and none of its bytes (rate-limit review r4 N-b). An embed's room (a `NoteSeat` parent, Epo 2026-10-20) joins only once its note's channel joined, naming that channel last in its JOIN; it ends with its note, reporting no close, and joins again naming the note's new channel; closed as the note's oldest embed (`collaboration-embed-closed`) it waits until `wake` (near the screen again). The room's `room-presence` message reaches `onPresence`, not the stateless handler, and goes empty when the channel ends; when the page sleeps (60 minutes idle, Epo 2026-10-20) the channel ends with no close or drop reported and the socket stays closed until `wake`, when the room joins again. While the `beforeJoin` promise holds (stored steps the room never accepted, Q327) no socket opens; the JOIN goes once it settles, and at once without one (Q360). In-place collection (Epo 2026-10-23): the JOIN names the stored version the document holds after its client id (0 when new, a document that took stored drafts names theirs), each `stored` is acknowledged with the version the tab reports, never above its oldest unsent edit (in flight, or held for a resend after its channel ended), nothing before it synced, and a Leave names its session; restored rows stored before versions join at 1, never 0 (L10). Review r1 (Editor 2026-10-26): an edit stays unsent until the second store's `stored` after its ACK, the channel's first notice answering its step 1 (H1, fails with an edit taken as stored at its ACK or first notice), also through a drop; an empty step 2 holds nothing back, so a brief open acknowledges its answer's version (H2), and a mark it answers clears by the H1 rule, not at the next edit (review r2 N1); an `ack` goes whenever the reportable version changes; drafts marked while connected (`unsentFrom`) ride the next update and clear by the same rule, and a Leave while they are marked says unsent (M2, N3); a document holding edits made before any stored version reports 1 (L8). |

## Collaboration Rust server (`collaboration-rs/crates/server`, `sources`, `ydoc`)

`pnpm test:collaboration` builds the notes markdown bundle and runs `cargo test` over the workspace in `collaboration-rs/` (the server is a binary crate: `--bins` for its unit tests alone). The integration tests need the docker e2e stack's Postgres, Redis and Go API (see the file headers); locally they skip without their variables. CI's `collaboration` job runs them all against that stack (`--include-ignored`, with `CAPY_IT_REQUIRED` making a missing variable a failure, and the `sources` DB tests failing without theirs), plus `cargo fmt`/`clippy` for the workspace's crates. Security regressions count work (`ydoc::steps`, yrs's own work counter, allocations), never wall-clock time; each was checked failing with its fix reverted (rust-core PROGRESS, security table).

| File | About |
| --- | --- |
| [`collaboration-rs/crates/server/src/auth.rs`](../collaboration-rs/crates/server/src/auth.rs) | Room names parse and print; a minted HS256 token verifies, and wrong rooms, expiry, access and signatures are refused; the service secret compares whole (security regression: collaboration token room binding and expiry); the client protocol minimum goes by the room family (material and keys rooms, source rooms); a token's client id and worker id are Yjs session ids (1 to 2^32-1), a worker id only with a client id and never equal to it (`a_tokens_client_ids_are_yjs_ids_and_its_worker_id_its_own`, Q226 L6). A stored draft token grants its ids only with our signature, for the same room and user, issued within 7 days (expiry ignored), and a send's first 16 tokens alone are read (`a_stored_token_grants_its_ids_only_for_its_room_and_user_within_7_days`, security regression: Q288, Q322). |
| [`collaboration-rs/crates/server/src/client_ids.rs`](../collaboration-rs/crates/server/src/client_ids.rs) | Admission of an update by client id: structs past what the room holds pass only under the writer's own ids, held structs (duplicates) and deletions of others' text pass, and an update under another user's id is refused (`only_the_writers_ids_may_add_structs`, security regression: Q213, catalogued for Q226 L6). A written id's row is refreshed at most once a day (`an_ids_writes_refresh_its_row_once_a_day`, r2 N1). |
| [`collaboration-rs/crates/server/src/sessions.rs`](../collaboration-rs/crates/server/src/sessions.rs) | A note room's editing sessions (in-place collection, step 1): the reached version is the oldest acknowledgement among counted sessions, an away session counts 24 h after it was last seen and ends then, a clean Leave ends one; each held deletion goes 25 h after it arrived (a batch takes its latest arrival) while its session still counts; only recorded sessions are written, each change once a store took it, an ended one cleared then forgotten; held batches round-trip; a session row whose held deletions cannot be read is dropped alone at load, the others load, and unreadable agent holds are dropped and written again cleared (Q382); a new session (version 0) that never synced is left out of the reached version and forgotten with its last channel, counted once synced (review r1 H2); **security regression** a live session is never taken by another user's JOIN, an ended one's id starts a new session (N4); a repeated `ack` writes nothing (L2); agent steps' deletions are held 25 h from the edit, an hour past its Undo (M3, review r3 N8), written and read back; a stored arrival rounds up to the second (N1); a store's version past an unapplied service edit leaves a gap, the room holding every version only up to it until the edit arrives (M1); late detection (a version below the window is late, a new session never, nothing before any collection; under a lost session's id always, review r2 M1, a damaged row's id and the ids loaded lost both remembered); a session that never acknowledged a store, holds nothing and has no row is forgotten with its last channel (r2 L1); another user's ack, deletion, Leave or end changes nothing (r2 N3); held deletions are written only when they changed (r2 L4). Each fails with its behaviour reverted. |

A JOIN carries the stored version after the client id (none from a source tab of an older build), and a Leave its clean byte and the session it names (in-place collection). |

A source room load is refused while loaded rooms' files fill the disk store (`a_source_room_is_refused_while_loaded_rooms_fill_the_disk_store`, Epo 2026-10-17): with the cap one byte short of a second text file, `/metrics` shows the first room's base and seed as `capy_collaboration_source_disk_held_bytes`, the second JOIN gets the retried `permission-denied`, counted once in `capy_collaboration_source_disk_refusals_total` and not in `capy_collaboration_authentication_failures_total`, and once the first room unloads its idle files make way and the second room loads. Under a lowered export cap (`ExportCap` sets every plan's `source_file_max_bytes` to 2 MiB and restores it on drop; such tests take turns), a text source whose base leaves no room (`a_source_room_refuses_growth_past_its_export_cap`, Epo 2026-10-17) closes the writer on its first keystroke with the byte-limit refusal, failing with the room's cap reverted to the shared 100 MB ceiling; and after an agent's 80 KiB edit a writer's 40 KiB that would fit only beside an uncounted agent edit is refused (`an_agent_edit_counts_toward_a_source_rooms_cap`), failing with `service_edit` not advancing the estimate. A text source the agent edited before its room ever saved takes a person's key inside the agent's text as the room's first save, which carries no seed and stores (`a_text_sources_first_save_after_an_agent_edit_carries_no_seed`; fails with the room still counting itself unsaved: the save merges the seed, refers to the edit's items the seed lacks and discards the room). The test client takes frames up to the source ceiling, as a browser does, instead of tungstenite's 16 MiB. An agent edit charges the note's payer, then waits on and stops for a payer whose deletion request commits mid-edit (review M4, N4). Link-shared viewers redeem the link first. A locked payer or actor refuses an agent edit at once while another transaction holds the material row (review N4, B5). The room's presence lists the people who can edit (an editor's reading tab too) by their signed tokens' name with the awareness client ids each holds, never by what an awareness claims, a person a number in the room and never a user id (a reader learns none), and an entry holds only avatar, clients, name and person (no device); a member hears every connection but its own (its user's other tab included) and a viewer is neither listed nor hears it (`the_rooms_presence_lists_editors_by_their_tokens_and_never_viewers`, security regression: Epo 2026-10-20; fails with viewers listed or sent it, a member's own connection listed, or a device field). ## Collaboration Rust notes crate (`collaboration-rs/crates/notes/`)

Parity tests against a corpus the Node collaboration server wrote (`tests/corpus/*.json.gz`, regenerated with `tests/corpus/generate.sh <checkout> [families]` from a checkout from before the Rust cutover, whose `collaboration/src` is the oracle). Run with `cargo test --release -p notes` in `collaboration-rs/`.

| File | About |
| ---- | ----- |
| [`collaboration-rs/crates/notes/tests/projection.rs`](../collaboration-rs/crates/notes/tests/projection.rs) | The Plate JSON projection of corpus notes (the near-limit load-test note, e2e and bench fixtures, marks, tables, voids, embeds) equals slate-yjs's, through `project` and `project_state`, and `slate_yjs::state_from_value` bootstraps a note whose projection is the value it was given. |
| [`collaboration-rs/crates/notes/tests/ops.rs`](../collaboration-rs/crates/notes/tests/ops.rs) | Random Slate operation sequences recorded through slate-yjs (15 corpus files: seed notes, the load note, an over-limit note, and small notes with marks, nesting, tables and voids) replay through the crate's editor and slate-yjs mapping: each step's Plate JSON, metrics and outcome equal Node's, and how many updates carry the same items is reported; an update Node took that the key rules refuse, or that writes a figure's `block` as one plain value (`PLAIN_BLOCK`: the Node-era writers' figures, Epo 2026-10-18), is counted as tightened and still applied as Node took it. |
| [`collaboration-rs/crates/notes/tests/bound.rs`](../collaboration-rs/crates/notes/tests/bound.rs) | Three writers on stale copies delivering merged or queued updates (`multi-1`..`multi-6`): every update's growth bound equals the JS bound, refusals and deferrals match, and the room's metrics and Plate JSON equal Node's; a delivery Node took and the key rule refuses (the corpus's writers insert blocks without ids) is counted and applied, and the validator re-measures. |
| [`collaboration-rs/crates/notes/tests/fuzz_admit.rs`](../collaboration-rs/crates/notes/tests/fuzz_admit.rs) | Deterministic mutation fuzz of the room path: 2,000 real updates (typing, deletes, a format, an attribute, new and removed blocks, a paste, three concurrent writers, items each naming a unit of a paragraph as their right origin, 40 chained clients, and items splitting every held item of a paragraph) with one to six bytes mutated (fixed xorshift seed) are decoded, admitted and, when admitted, applied, measured and projected; it fails on a panic, on admission walks over 4 steps per byte of the update and the room (counted, not timed), or on a case with structs counting no step, and prints the case. `FUZZ_CASES` and `FUZZ_SEED` run more. |
| [`collaboration-rs/crates/notes/tests/yjs_traffic.rs`](../collaboration-rs/crates/notes/tests/yjs_traffic.rs) | Traffic made by Yjs 13.6.31 itself (`corpus/yjs-traffic.cjs`: 60 seeds of 2-6 docs editing nested blocks, delivered as reconnect diffs, draft-run, overlapping and cross-doc `Y.mergeUpdates` bundles, 3,641 deliveries with fixed client ids) is admitted or unheld, never refused, except deliveries the key rule refuses because the generator inserts blocks without an id and sets their type in a later transaction (counted; the note editor writes an element with its type and id in one); so are the six deliveries the round 8 placement replay refused or miscounted (`corpus/yjs-review4-pairs.json`). |

A writer's 8-byte update deleting all 32,000 plain attributes of one paragraph stays inline (`heavy` false) and goes in within 4 steps per byte for `heavy` and admission alike, with no entry lookup (`Walk::Entries`) for keys no element requires; the checks read an element's entries only through that counted lookup, and the test refuses a scan of an element's map in `limits.rs`, which the steps could not count (the M3 scan took 89 s in debug) (security regression: REVIEW5 M3, seconds of key checks on an async worker). |

The legacy `image` type is refused as a type the embed catalog does not list. An image, audio or file element without its asset id, with an empty one, or with a `url` or `src` is refused when the update arrives, whether the update brings the element, sets the URL on an image, makes a paragraph an image or deletes the asset id; one naming its asset, or replacing it, goes in (Epo 2026-10-10; security regression: REVIEW5 N1, an update the store would refuse and so discard the room). A `src` set on a held paragraph takes no copy of the room and stays inline, while a URL set on an image is checked on one copy off the async workers (`limits::heavy`; security regression: REVIEW5 M1, a room copy per 16-byte update on a tokio worker). An update that leaves an element without a key the store requires is refused at admission with no copy: a deleted `type`, a deleted top-level `id`, a new top-level block without an id or a type, a paragraph made a reference without its material id, a reference's material id deleted; a deleted optional key, a new block with its keys, a retyped heading and deleted whole blocks go in (security regression: REVIEW5 R2, an update the store refuses discarded the room for every editor). A writer that already wrote pastes several blocks and an image, and it goes in (the checks no longer ask yrs for a clock the room has not seen, which panicked) (security regression: REVIEW5 recheck, a yrs index panic in the key and media checks). A `type` overwritten with the new entry deleted in the same update (a writer's two updates merged), and a stale lower client's losing `type` sent with a delete of the current one, are refused on the bound and exact paths; the losing write alone goes in, read on the trial copy such an update gets, with no copy of its own (security regression: REVIEW5 R2b, a block left without its type discarded the room). The reviewer's 21-byte crafted small edit, two `type` entries after one, is inline by size yet `heavy` (its key check reads the result), goes in and takes one key copy (security regression: REVIEW5 final S2, that copy on an async worker, repeatably); with a refusal beside it (25 bytes), `heavy` and admit agree on 100 runs: refused inline, no copy (security regression: REVIEW5 final S1, the check stopped in a random order at the first element needing a copy).A new reference carrying an imported fence body (`pending`), one set on a held reference and a new reference without its material id are refused at admit, as the store check refuses them (security regression: live-items REVIEW5 pending references; fails without the `pending` refusal or with an empty material id holding). A reference created or retyped below the top level (a quoted reference, a quote line retyped) is refused at admit as the store refuses it, while a top-level one goes in (live-items REVIEW5 R2; fails without the check). |

## Playwright app copy (`e2e/i18n/`)

Every Playwright config (e2e, UAT, editor, bench/editor) imports `e2e/i18n/compile.ts`, which compiles `messages/` into the ignored `e2e/.paraglide` when it is older than `messages/` (built in a temporary folder and swapped in, so parallel runs never read a half-written folder); `pnpm test:uat:verifier` runs it first too. Specs import `m` from `e2e/i18n` and locate app copy with `m.*`; state assertions read component data attributes (`data-save-state`, `data-sort`/`data-order`, `data-resend`, `data-result`, `data-block-type`, `data-block-style`, `data-privacy`, `data-share-role`, `data-unread-count`, `data-width`, `data-slide`, the save banner's `data-kind`, `ErrorState`'s `data-error-kind` read by `expectErrorSurface`) instead of displayed text. Seed data, typed text, MathLive and BetterOffice labels stay literal.

## Playwright e2e — real stack (`e2e/errors/`, `e2e/sharing/`, `e2e/study/`)

Real stack via Docker (`pnpm e2e`). Editor specs are ignored by the root Playwright config. CI runs it as
its own job (`e2e_stack`) and prebuilds the collaboration and server images
with the GitHub Actions layer cache, so `E2E_PREBUILT_IMAGES=true` starts the
stack with `--no-build`; locally the setup still runs `up --build`.

E2E tests check functional outcomes and may select individual UI elements. They
do not enforce UI layout, DOM wrapper structure, or section/menu organization.
Authorization rules (who gets 401, 404 or 403) are asserted in Go
(`server/internal/httpapi/share_access_test.go` and its neighbours); these
browser suites cover what users see.

Shared upload inputs belong in [`e2e/fixtures/files/`](../e2e/fixtures/files/README.md).
Its guide describes scenario sets, format-specific edits, and expected persisted
results. The heavy UAT lifecycle runner explicitly selects its fixture cases; adding
files alone does not execute them. New local E2E coverage should prioritize upload and
processing failures, with provider failures injected in the isolated test stack.

The four local workers open up to eight Chromium contexts against one Vite dev
server and the Dockerized API. On a machine that cannot absorb that, API
responses stretch to several seconds and the editor takes tens of seconds to
reach `Synced`, so budgets calibrated for a healthy host expire — the collab and
material-mode specs fail even though the flows complete. Use `pnpm e2e:slow`
(one worker) there; it is a host-capacity workaround, not a fix for a flaky spec.

## Playwright e2e — authorized UAT (`e2e/uat/`)

Opt-in: a **Deploy UAT** run only probes service health. These run on a manual
**Deterministic UAT quality** dispatch and as the production promotion gate.

Remote Chromium against an explicitly authorized UAT deployment
(`pnpm e2e:uat`). It requires the dedicated Clerk UAT keys, five synthetic
account emails, and private fixture IDs described in
[`deployment-runbook.md`](deployment-runbook.md#12-uat-review-environment-and-external-service-sandboxes).
It never starts or targets the local E2E auth-bypass stack.
The authorization configuration excludes `journeys/`. The separate manual
critical-path suite uploads through the UAT server and uses the shared
nonproduction ingest project. See the [journey setup and cleanup guide](../e2e/uat/journeys/README.md).

| File                                                                | About                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [`e2e/uat/authorization.spec.ts`](../e2e/uat/authorization.spec.ts) | Short-lived Clerk Backend API sign-in tokens create real sessions that verify private-workspace visibility, non-disclosing unrelated-user denial, owner/editor workspace statistics, and collaboration-token modes across accounts (owner and editor write, viewer read for live View, unrelated account 404). |

Supporting configuration: [`e2e/uat/playwright.uat.config.ts`](../e2e/uat/playwright.uat.config.ts)
fails closed unless authorization is exactly `true`, all UAT hosts are explicitly
allowed, URL schemes are secure, and every Clerk key, synthetic identity, and
fixture ID is present. CI retains trace, screenshot, video, and HTML evidence
only for the configured artifact window.

The heavy suite (`pnpm e2e:uat:journeys`) has twenty-eight cases (plus one fixme, one manual journey and one Office load measurement outside the lanes)
in lanes (Playwright projects `office`, `app` and `billing`, plus `refresh` for the planned
refresh journeys) that the workflow runs as parallel jobs, each with its own run
id, one worker and no whole-journey retries. Normal CI and lightweight deploy checks exclude it;
manual quality defaults it on and production promotion requires it. Assertions
use backend/storage/provider outcomes, with browser controls used for actions.
Only the Office load measurement records traces (with screenshots); no journey
records video. Sanitized manifests and cleanup reports are retained for 30 days.

edit and for the target's text cursor before clicking and typing, since remote
layout updates briefly gate hit testing while the accessibility mirror remains.

epoch in the run's sanitized evidence instead of relying on truncated ZIP bytes.

PPTX journey pastes through the real clipboard into the native text input and
checks the exported text. Native tests cover composition; the live journey
does not drive an operating-system IME or provide a slide-text accessibility
mirror. The [September 27 investigation](../artifacts/2026-09-25-office-progress/investigation-2026-09-27.md)
records the original failures, and the [Astra review](../artifacts/2026-09-25-office-progress/review-astra-xhigh-2026-09-27.md)
records the fixes and their verification.

## Playwright e2e — editor feature matrix (`e2e/editor/`)

`floating-toolbar.spec.ts` checks that selection and link actions move with their text synchronously during scrolling, before Floating UI or React position updates can run; top-toolbar formatting keeps the selection toolbar mounted and open, while collapsed selections still dismiss it.

MSW + Vite only (`pnpm e2e:msw:editor`); no Docker. CI runs it in two shards
(`e2e_editor`, `--shard=N/2`) in parallel with the real-stack job. The editor project uses
full Chromium's headless mode because the separate headless shell can strand
modified-click tabs ([Playwright #42142](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/42142)).

CI uploads both browser suites' reports and failure traces for seven days,
including failed attempts whose retry succeeds.
The Office save-recovery scenarios allow two minutes overall for native
initialization and a full Vite reload; their individual assertion deadlines
remain unchanged.

| File                                                                                | About                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

stability in the icon picker, workspace edit/create and task edit dialogs.

## Playwright perf (`bench/editor/`)

MSW + Vite (`pnpm bench:editor`). 6 cases total: 4 budget specs always run; 2 diagnostic V8 profiles are skipped unless `PERF_PROFILE=1`. Budgets are regression tripwires under CPU throttle, not UX targets. How to run the suite, what the GHA snapshot compare does, and why deltas stay warn-only: [editor-perf.md](editor-perf.md).

| [`bench/editor/scripts/saveCycleProfile.perf.ts`](../bench/editor/scripts/saveCycleProfile.perf.ts) | 1 case, opt-in (`PERF_PROFILE=1`): V8 CPU profile of the near-limit save cycle (diagnostic, no budget assert).                                          |
| [`bench/editor/scripts/typingProfile.perf.ts`](../bench/editor/scripts/typingProfile.perf.ts)       | 1 case, opt-in (`PERF_PROFILE=1`): V8 CPU profile of idle, heading typing, and body typing with per-suspect attribution (diagnostic, no budget assert). |

| File                                                                    | About                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`bench/editor/scripts/runtime.office.ts`](../bench/editor/scripts/runtime.office.ts) | 26 cases. Per file (small and large DOCX, XLSX and PPTX): open to first paint, View to Edit ready and its first painted frame (report-only for XLSX/PPTX), keystroke to painted frame at the start and (report-only) at the end of the file, and heap after each: JS, the frames' WASM per module, each worker's JS and WASM (the DOCX engine); a co-editor case (ten remote edits from the mock room as a second peer: queue, in-frame synchronous apply (DOCX: hand-off only), receipt to paint or next frame, long tasks; report-only); worker memory only after the budgeted steps; then heap over two full view-mode passes; for the small files and the long DOCX, heap after each of five view-mode closes. XLSX also: a peer's 8,000-cell paste and row insert and the same done locally (long tasks and delay to the painted grid), typing twenty values while a peer pastes and inserts a row (every value lands, the selection walks on), and scrolling a 50,000-row sheet (paints and frames per second); report-only. Every result records the runner's CPU. Fails on unpainted keys, typing that sends no edit (at either end), a remote edit that never arrives or paints or a runtime error, a viewer or editor `ready` without timings, a worker fallback or a missed budget (calibrated on CI, 30 ms keystroke floor); heap is report-only. Runs in the `Performance` workflow's `office` job (dispatch only). |

Fails on non-convergence, a missing or doubled marker or a collaboration error in any room, exit 2 on a missed first-phase p95 budget (calibrated on CI). ## Manual / diagnostic (not in CI suites)

Query freshness check: notifications and workspace chapter, file, and material
lists use a five-second stale time with focus refetching; other queries inherit
the five-minute default unless they declare an override. Workspace list route
prefetches use the same five-second options as their hooks.
File and material details also use five seconds: reopen a cached item after
five seconds to check its refresh, and verify tab focus alone does not refetch it.

Workspace-list cache check: in MSW, reload `/workspaces` and verify one
`GET /api/workspaces?sort=accessed` request. The route loader and page use
`{ sort: 'accessed', tag: [] }` to share the prefetched cache entry.

Workspace source-preview check: in MSW Biology 101, click `Biology notes - pending.md`
and `Biology notes - processing.md` in the file list. Both should open their
Markdown content while retaining the processing progress banner. These fixtures
have uploaded bytes but are not indexed yet.

| File                                                                                                | About                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`knowledge_base_pilot.py`](../bench/rag/scripts/knowledge_base_pilot.py), [`knowledge_base_realtime.py`](../bench/rag/scripts/knowledge_base_realtime.py), [`knowledge_base_common.py`](../bench/rag/scripts/knowledge_base_common.py), [`test_knowledge_base_pilot.py`](../bench/rag/scripts/test_knowledge_base_pilot.py) | Local three-book parsing, embeddings and isolated pgvector pilot. Model stages run through `--provider ollama` (GLM-5.3-Flash on the local Ollama cloud model) or `tokenhub` with a 429 backoff; `knowledge_base_realtime.prepare` freezes a stage's requests and earlier Batch receipts stay readable as local files (the Batch client is deleted). Tests cover provider dispatch, endpoint-switching retries, `run_topics`, optional `proposed_topic` and accepted tag failures of any kind. The summaries stage is deleted; `tag_outputs`/`tags_document` are the shared `tags.json` writer the builder's tag stage imports, and `evidence_verified` is the shared tolerant verifier (case, whitespace, ellipsis with every piece verbatim) both use. Frozen 24-query A/B comparison adds role/topic tags to hybrid candidates. A short `Figure N:` line under a centred diagram merges into its `vector_drawing` record (caption, caption box, block index, section path, the excluded flag its caption box names, and the excerpt link through the caption) with no `caption_page_reference` left, while a caption too far below keeps its own record. Run `node lab/knowledge/tests/download-filter.cjs`. |

manual NonCommercial rejection API preserves licence evidence and refuses non-403 and active/downloaded items; the licence gate table including US jurisdiction suffixes, NC/ND exclusions and GNU aliases, worker failure cause preservation, and irrelevant rejection before licence checks, subject schema accepting parent subjects and rejecting invented IDs; catalog-only discovery and individual-book metadata gating, authorless downloads and reviewed authorless admission/manifest/publication checks, Free Courseware title/filename rejection including queued downloads, source-bound PDF/follow links and licence quotes, preserving anchor text/ARIA labels/title/image alt and merging duplicate URL labels, direct PDFs refusing inherited metadata, HTML content negotiation, mixed HTTP/HTTPS links and same-catalog pagination preserving depth; redirects followed by hand with every hop's host checked for non-public addresses (security regression: builder scraper redirects); the dashboard's Host allowlist and `X-Capy-Builder` header (security regression: builder Host/header guard); figure matching by label then order; descriptions on the excerpt's first chunk `indexed_text` only; the live path aligning, holding, skipping and describing; accept and reject with an empty span refused; a page failing both live passes failing the stage; `--redo` sending every page again); the tag stage (the tolerant verifier table, eight per request with a missing excerpt re-sent singly, `tags.json` equal to `apply_tags` on the same outputs, the 2% ceiling, the candidate prefix and evidence rule); the ingest runner (pause, failure, retry, dependency refusal pausing the workflow, publish refusing undecided held chunks, the source upload using only the writer key (security regression: library writer key), `books.json` export); ## Site Worker and deployment configuration

UAT's scriptless API route is an edge configuration check, separate from Worker
unit tests. The [deployment runbook](deployment-runbook.md#101-uat-api-routing-without-workers)
describes API/authenticated SSE probes, preserved cache/security headers, summary
and asset checks, and a Worker tail proving `/api/*` bypasses execution.

### Native OpenDataLoader accuracy experiments

These manual, benchmark-only checks preserve the production parser and chunker.
See the [accuracy follow-up](../bench/parsers/reports/2026-09-09-odl-accuracy-followup.md)
for measured scope and source evidence.

Explicit `--pdf`, `--parsed`, `--output` replays source accessibility alternatives into exact-matching cached blocks, checks page-99 distances and all answer associations, preserves failed/abstained cases, and probes in-memory ActualText extraction. Counts are intervention counts, not whole-book accuracy; no model, service, or source writes. |
| [`experiment_prince_headings.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_prince_headings.py) | `--self-check` and six-book cached replay compare folio-less margin-banner removal, complete outline-root matching, full-outline remapping and rejected front-matter name demotion. Measures breadcrumb ancestry, body coverage, outline-heading retention and changed canonical chunks; no parsing service or embeddings. |
| [`experiment_prince_math_loss.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_prince_math_loss.py) | Frozen source-region detector experiment for vector/raster content missing from native text, with negative controls, synthetic raster probes, raw-chunk reason propagation and actual passage-header visibility. Optional `--whole-book` measures warning volume and runtime. Region detection does not establish formula recall or recovery accuracy. |

No library writes, automatic retries, images or material review. |
| [`compare_mineru_pipeline_local.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/compare_mineru_pipeline_local.py), [`review_mineru_pipeline_local.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/review_mineru_pipeline_local.py) | Hash-frozen, byte-identical 28-page PDF slices compare current refined ODL with explicit MinerU pipeline, CPU-only, two serialized passes. Preserves parser wall times and native artifacts; the review command runs current packing/heading/confidence code for separate source inspection. Diagnostic cases cover formulas, table values/scopes, false heading roles and an OCR-layer scan. No model APIs or indexing; selected slices do not estimate whole-book accuracy, and MinerU confidence is an uncalibrated compatibility diagnostic. |
| [`structure_chunking_eval.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/structure_chunking_eval.py), [`structure_chunking_embed.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/structure_chunking_embed.py), [`structure_chunking_jlpt_eval.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/structure_chunking_jlpt_eval.py) | Frozen PDF boundary/relationship experiments measuring chunk counts, source anchors, term coverage and gold-page retrieval, with a separate fresh-embedding comparison and replay of the original JLPT query vectors. Native parsing and authorized embedding calls use isolated benchmark resources; page hits and term coverage are not answer-accuracy measurements. |
| [`section_boundary_eval.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/section_boundary_eval.py) | Paired current-pipeline packing and adjacent native list/table boundaries across 13 complete PDFs, with fixed anchor/cleanliness probes and hash-bound embedding reuse. Declares separate eight-source locator and 13-source legacy/JLPT query pools; source-page overlap is a retrieval proxy, not answer accuracy. |
| [`experiment_odl_font_recovery.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_font_recovery.py) | `check` validates literal embedded Type1 encoding, narrow contradictory-map eligibility and explicit glyph-derived cmap output. `prepare/run/score` audit sources, compare fresh Java output and rendered-pixel identity, and check frozen numeric rows and prose identifiers. |
| [`experiment_odl_native_improvements.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_native_improvements.py) | Manual `freeze/parse/improve/audit` experiment with fresh Java output, source-defined table rows, actual chunks, rejected extraction/replacement variants, double-overprint evidence and separate source controls. Reports structural associations separately from flat-text and chunk retention. |
| [`experiment_odl_layout_ocr.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_layout_ocr.py) | Historical: imports `parser/odl/ocr.py`, which the 2026-10-15 VLM change removed, so it no longer runs against the current parser. It was a manual real PP-OCRv6/PP-DocLayoutV3 comparison with frozen source-region order, negative controls, complete line permutations and actual chunk artifacts (`score` needed no models; `table-rows` preserved a rejected development variant). Its diagnostic corpus results never certified unseen-layout accuracy. |
| [`validate_odl_repairs.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/validate_odl_repairs.py) | Source/gold freeze for four new publisher families, explicit raw Java and production-matched baselines, candidate native/fresh-OCR runs, saved-output scoring and final packing. Preserves source/script/model hashes and failed receipts; reports scoped row/cell text and region ordering separately from unscored header semantics. |
| [`verify_odl_runtime.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/verify_odl_runtime.py) | Explicit loopback/container/spool verification of whole-document artifacts, FIFO capacity (executing up to `parse_workers`, the rest queued), hard-timeout and OOM quarantine. Records responses, health/cgroup measurements and bundle entry counts and sizes (v5 bundles carry no images); never starts services or contacts the shared ingest host. |
| [`experiment_odl_reading_order.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_reading_order.py) | `--self-check` validates conservative column ordering, unchanged blocks, source-confirmed rotated headings, same-font sentence continuations including list tails, and preservation of page/region geometry. Selected experiment flags are `--move-rotated --split-continuations`. Requires PyMuPDF 1.28.2. |
| [`experiment_odl_native_tables.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_native_tables.py) | `--check` covers exact native header/title/unit packing, shared body-cell scope, citation coverage, cross-page rejection and explicit ordinary packing for unsupported native tables. Corpus replay compares production, existing structured, strict context and bounded context arms. |
| [`experiment_odl_source_styles.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_source_styles.py) | `--check` distinguishes yellow, white and blue cell backgrounds, rejects later opaque fills and preserves caller data. Corpus replay retains literal source-confirmed yellow cell annotations and records strict structured-packing failures separately. Requires PyMuPDF 1.28.2. |
| [`replay_odl_accuracy.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/replay_odl_accuracy.py) | Composes explicitly selected saved font, reading-order and cell-style outputs before bounded native table packing. Rejects baseline mismatches, case-set differences and overlapping edits; records input/output/source hashes. This is an offline interaction check, not a combined latency benchmark. |
| [`experiment_odl_heading_context.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_heading_context.py) | `--check` builds real PDF spans to verify numeric footer sequences, rotated chapter tabs, repeated banners and metadata conservation. Saved-output replay scores actual chunks, section paths and indexed text against frozen source checks; selected arm `structure` preserves continuing sections across pages. Requires PyMuPDF 1.28.2. |
| [`experiment_odl_ocr_disagreement.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_ocr_disagreement.py) | Positional `check` verifies fragment matching, native column order, protected pages and idempotence. `prepare/ocr/replay` retain source gates and rejected OCR variants. The selected repair reorders native blocks on eligible hidden OCR-layer pages; automatic OCR text replacement was rejected. |
| [`experiment_odl_table_geometry.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_table_geometry.py) | `--check` covers ruled-region selection, row/header geometry, row-label spans and partial-overlap abstention. Ruled-table extraction and optional `--row-label-spans` remain bounded experiments, outside the integrated arms. Replacement rejects partially overlapping or unpositioned native blocks; explicit oracle overrides do not establish a safe repair. Requires PyMuPDF 1.28.2. |
| [`measure_odl_native_pipeline.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/measure_odl_native_pipeline.py) | `root output --variant baseline\|native\|extended\|refined` runs fresh Java parsing, adaptation and one chunk pass with source hashes, snapshots, phase timings and memory sampling. Native adds the four first-pass repairs; extended adds source-backed headings and native hidden-layer column order; refined composes the third-pass source repairs and explicit footer ancestry. Detector/header controls are explicit experiments with unchanged defaults. Run sequentially on an idle VM. Excludes OCR, captions, indexing and application queues. |
| [`score_odl_font_transfer.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/score_odl_font_transfer.py) | `root pdf checks output` scores completed neighboring-paper font runs against frozen numeric sequences and the clean-font control, retaining raw and chunk evidence. Value recovery does not certify row/header associations or table semantics. |
| [`score_odl_native_pipeline.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/score_odl_native_pipeline.py) | `local output` verifies all three measured arms across three repeats and eight documents/254 pages, source/output hashes, content conservation, frozen heading checks, Japanese native table context, prior source-scored chunks and German/NIST continuations. Produces a new verification JSON from completed artifacts. |
| [`experiment_odl_native_text.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_native_text.py) | `--check` and corpus replay validate source-confirmed overprint deletion and paragraph-role repair, exact unedited blocks/geometry, idempotence and frozen actual-chunk checks. The original frozen helper handles text blocks. |
| [`experiment_odl_heading_retention.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_heading_retention.py) | Replays source-visible orphan-heading retention after chunking, preserving every existing chunk and adding literal source text with source boxes; source checks reject OCR footers and already-indexed labels, including terminal hyphens at section/body boundaries. |
| [`experiment_odl_exponents.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_exponents.py) | `--sources MANIFEST --output NEW_DIR` checks source-bound scientific exponents, unchanged geometry and caller fields, caret-only edits and idempotence. Writes actual chunks and per-occurrence source evidence. |
| [`experiment_odl_math_recovery.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_math_recovery.py) | Isolated OCR consensus, layout detection, formula recognition and replay retain fixed source crops, automatic detection, negative controls and actual-chunk formula/prose checks. Recognition runs require the VM model runtimes. |
| [`experiment_odl_table_integration.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_table_integration.py) | `--check` and full-source scans audit extraction separately from automatic replacement, retain all rejected candidates, and verify unchanged blocks/furniture/chunks. Frozen failed candidates remain evidence, not approved parser behavior. |
| [`score_odl_independent.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/score_odl_independent.py) | `--check` rejects changed row values and invented missing values. `--checks FIXTURE --runs RUN_DIR... --output JSON` compares frozen row/prose sequences in native output and actual chunks; complete table meaning and formulas require the separate source rubric. |
| [`experiment_odl_list_text.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_list_text.py) | Reuses the source overprint proof for list items while preserving item and whitespace boundaries; includes legitimate repetition and boundary ambiguity controls. |
| [`experiment_odl_list_geometry.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_list_geometry.py) | Requires exact Java list identity and source binding before unioning same-page text-bearing descendant boxes; checks excluded descendants, geometry-only text conservation, final citations and idempotence. |
| [`experiment_odl_column_continuation.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/experiment_odl_column_continuation.py) | Moves a complete continuation only when source text, column geometry and font evidence distinguish intervening small print; preserves every block and checks actual prose chunks. |
| [`refine_odl_output.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/refine_odl_output.py) | Composes source-bound native repairs before one final chunk pass, preserving rejected candidates and phase evidence. Fresh parsing runs through `measure_odl_native_pipeline.py --variant refined`; explicit alternate detector and header/footer controls preserve existing runner defaults. |
| [`score_odl_refined.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/score_odl_refined.py) | Applies frozen text, list, section-context, retention and NIST-fragment diagnostics to either parser's final chunks, retaining individual verdicts and input hashes. These narrow checks do not certify full-document accuracy. |

[`evaluate_odl_table_geometry.py`](../bench/parsers/scripts/evaluate_odl_table_geometry.py)
in `integrate` mode replays the eight source-reviewed
tables through conservative and explicit manual-override replacement. Its `score`
mode checks complete source grids, actual document chunks, retained blocks and
the disclosed source-rubric correction. It uses the fixed retained experiment
inputs; it does not evaluate every accepted geometry region. The measured
pipeline scorer also accepts `--extended-prefix` to verify equivalent later
source-inspection variants against the original expanded output.

record scope and limitations. The
[parser benchmark README](../bench/parsers/README.md#native-opendataloader-second-pass)
lists executable focused checks, measurement commands and evidence-scoring
commands; scorers require the retained local artifacts and fresh output paths.

### Question bank and shared question format

- `e2e/editor/question-bank-paging.spec.ts`: the bank loads a long mock topic 10 questions at a time, a tree square click on an unloaded question loads its page plus the next in one request and scrolls it to the panel top, then questions 11–20 load above on their own without moving it; scrolled up to question 11, questions 1–10 wait while a (synthetic) finger is down and go in without moving the reading position once it lifts. Run `pnpm run e2e:slow --config=e2e/editor/playwright.editor.config.ts question-bank-paging.spec.ts`.
- `e2e/editor/question-bank-answering.spec.ts`: in view mode a typed answer is checked, its review shows the part score and accepted answers, the tree's square for it turns right, and Try again clears the field; the /qb landing shows the latest topic's progress line and a Finished list, "Continue at question 5" opens the next unanswered question, and the page's Partially wrong status filter narrows the topic to its one question; a finished topic's summary shows its score and the wrong count, and a red square opens its question. Run `pnpm run e2e:slow --config=e2e/editor/playwright.editor.config.ts question-bank-answering.spec.ts`.
- `e2e/editor/question-dialog.spec.ts`: in a live quiz's question dialog, Undo right after adding a chart (its editor still open, its edits staged until Done) takes the block back and the dialog returns to the question; in a note's embedded quiz, adding a block refetches the quiz (the note footer's read of the same query borrows the embed's queryFn) and the question dialog stays open; the dialog's close button, with an answer editor open, goes back to the question rather than closing; a part's row selects on a click and opens its answer on a double click; a part's marks step with + and hold to the marks cap (20) when typed past it; a multiple choice option's mark-as-correct toggle (after its trash button) presses and releases; a table block adds a column and removes a row with the controls under it; adding a part keeps the question shown, with the new part's answer in it. Run `pnpm run e2e:slow --config=e2e/editor/playwright.editor.config.ts question-dialog.spec.ts`.
- `e2e/editor/question-formula.spec.ts`: real MathLive inside the question Plate editor (opened by an outline row, which focuses the block, then Enter) accepts a physical digit and retains it after commit/reopen, guarding against Slate canceling MathLive input; native menu templates also insert inside the question dialog. Question viewing and editing previews use inert MathLive with matching conjugate/derivative/plain-text dimensions. Block note editing preserves height; its ghost toggle, Escape and outside clicks dismiss the keyboard, keyboard taps still enter digits, and commit cleans it up. Inline question editing omits the keyboard toggle. At 360 px (the smallest supported phone) the quiz editor's reaction equation, wider than its column, scrolls sideways in its own box under the wheel while no scroller around it and not the page overflows; its `scroll-fade-x` edges read 0px/28px at rest and 28px/0px scrolled to the end, and reopened at 1440 px, where it fits, its box has no fade and `mask-image: none`. A click on a question formula selects it (no editor opens) and Delete removes it; a double click edits it. Run `pnpm run e2e:slow --config=e2e/editor/playwright.editor.config.ts question-formula.spec.ts`.
- `server/internal/questions/blank_test.go`: a question counts as blank only when every part is empty (whitespace, empty gaps, no matched pair), not with a chosen option or `false`, and never with an ordering part.
- `server/internal/questions/score_test.go`: the shared scoring fixtures in `server/internal/questions/testdata/scoring/` (mcq sets with one or several correct options, boolean, fuzzy short answers with the JavaScript string rules, exact quantities, whole-order ordering, matching and gaps per item with half marks; also read by the `grade.ts` Vitest), a learner view of malformed stored content, and `Graded` awarding every part without touching the stored question.
- `server/internal/questions/questions_test.go`, `collaboration-rs/crates/notes/tests/validation.rs`, `src/features/questions/validation.test.ts`: shared valid/invalid fixtures for the seven answer types (an mcq with several correct options, `mcq-several-correct.json`; an open part with no sample answer, `open-no-sample.json`, and two refused, `open-two-samples-rejected.json`), bank asset policy, quiz editor-asset images, user-quiz part/marking-item/sample-answer bounds (the bank keeps its own), gap answers (one non-empty accepted list per gap, blanks (1)…(n) in the text matching them), graph references (including angles, arcs, sectors and polygons, repeated points, a centre that is also an endpoint, and segment `ticks` within 1–3)/static SVG, quantity units/zero denominator, Unicode bounds, part marks (required, a marking scheme only on open parts with items that add up to the part's marks, no zero-mark or string items) and attempt-only awards. `questions_test.go` also covers quiz-wide part and open-part caps and the Go grading text (stem, earlier parts, figures, tables, chart data). It also checks that a quiz figure may link only under the bank's asset base (`QuizBankAssetsURL`), and only when one is set; `validation.test.ts` checks the same in the browser under `VITE_BANK_ASSETS_URL`. The Go validator names the part and the rule when a closed part carries a markscheme. A chart with an empty category label is valid in every validator (`chart-description.json`), as are an image without a description (`quiz-image-no-description.json`) and a one-point scatter (`plot-scatter-one-point.json`), while a one-point line is refused (`plot-line-one-point-rejected.json`); a plot's title, axis titles and unit at 100 code points and its series names and line and mark labels at 60 are valid (`plot-at-limits.json`, astral and CJK characters counted once), and a 101-character title, a 61-character series name and a 61-character mark label are refused (`plot-long-*-rejected.json`, Epo 2026-10-17); a chart with null values (bar and pie, `chart-null-value.json`) is valid and a series short of its labels is refused (`chart-short-series-rejected.json`; the normalisers pad before validating); the Go grading text writes a figure without a description as `[Figure]`. Plot blocks are tested in Go (`TestPlotBlockBoundsAndGradingText`: curves, points, reference lines and marks within bounds, and the grading text listing points and labels) and in `validation.test.ts` with the same cases, outside the shared fixtures, which the removed Node server generated; the Rust validator tests the same cases in `validation.rs` (`a_plot_validates_as_go_validates_it`). Go's `questions.RepairFigure` (its index text's) follows the shared figure repair fixtures (`testdata/repairs/figures.json`) and leaves its input as it was (Epo 2026-10-18).
- `src/features/questions/types.test.ts`: `withGapsText` keeps each blank's accepted answers with it and renumbers the part's later blanks when a text gains a blank; `withoutGapsBlock` drops a removed text's blanks and their answers and renumbers the rest.
- `src/features/questions/parseMathText.test.ts`, `TextEditor.test.ts`, `graph.test.ts`, `graphSyntax.test.ts`, `src/components/charts/CategoryChart.test.tsx`, `PlotChart.test.tsx`: math-token boundaries and editor serialization (a gaps part's blanks read as chips and written numbered from the block's start), safe graph expressions/export recipe, label wrapping and GeoGebra tick steps and numbers, Desmos-style graph rows to recipe elements and back (scientific numbers as `m·10ⁿ`) and rows following a peer's rebased elements (`syncRows`: the same rows when nothing changed, a row still being typed kept in place), shared chart rendering (a null value draws nothing in every chart kind, a line breaking at it; a pie or stacked chart without a positive value and a chart without series draw the empty frame), and a plot's clean ticks, x-ordered curve, dashed reference line and labelled points (a plot without series draws the empty frame).
- `src/features/questions/PlotEditor.test.ts`: the note plot editor's round trip: a series renamed and a point moved through the editor's own inputs give the block the note dialog saves (no issue, and the block schema parses it unchanged), and an emptied cell gives the plot's issue ("Plot error: …"); new rows come filled from the row before them (a point, a horizontal line, a labelled point) and a new series from [0, 0] and [1, 1] on a line or [0, 0] on a scatter, leaving no issue. A merged plot's series past the cap and a line's one-point series are marked in the editor and named by `blockIssues` (Epo 2026-10-18).
- `src/features/notes/blocks/plotFence.test.ts`: a ` ```plot ` fence in agent markdown becomes a valid `plot` node whose fence body writes the same block back, and a plot the block schema refuses fails the conversion.

- `src/features/quizzes/QuestionRunner.test.tsx`: a server-graded review renders its part scores as given, the answer before a collapsed solution, and fixed units; open parts show one Jev mark per marking item and a correct, partial or skipped verdict over their marking points; matching answered by option text on a shuffled learner view offers letter buttons as well as the menu and letters the stored options on review with the chosen and correct letters; an ordering answered by item text keeps the learner's order and lists the correct order with where each misplaced item was put.

- `src/features/study/railMap/map.test.ts`: Learning's railway map is the same for a workspace and different for another, keeps its drawing when items are added (except near the old terminus), never orders two dense biomes together or a city beside open country, fills a panel wider than a short workspace, keeps every desktop view under 120 elements, wraps station names on two lines with an ellipsis, and its stored density labels match `measure()`.
- `src/features/study/finishToasts.test.ts`: the finish toast fires for a topic or workspace finished by a progress refetch (including a topic first listed already finished, or one reopened by new questions and finished again) and not for one finished before.
- `src/features/questions/trailMap/map.test.ts`: the /qb progress map is the same for a topic and different for another, keeps its drawing when questions are added (except the last stretch before the old summit), never orders two dense biomes together, three sparse in a row or more than three without a dense one, keeps the busiest desktop view under 80 elements, and its stored biome density labels match `measure()`.
- `src/features/questions/bankSearch.test.ts`: the /qb panel search returns exams, subjects and topics separately, each matched by its own name and ranked a name's start before a later word, then a match inside (an exam's description counting from the word-start rank), and leaves out an exam's hidden one subject and a single-topic exam's topic.
- `src/features/questions/QuestionView.test.tsx`: the review answer line typesets bare-LaTeX accepted answers and joins a plain `°` unit to each accepted value while other units keep the space; a one-part question shows its marks once, in the header.

- `server/internal/review/review_test.go`: answer histories weigh in the order Epo signed off (eight correct answers add nothing, a single first miss leans on "not known yet"); question scores map to Again below 0.5, Hard below 0.7, otherwise Good; a lapsed item ranks as less retained and a miss on a new item counts as a lapse; the question hash covers only the stem and part prompt text, not answers, marking schemes, marks, layout or images; question scores use part marks with half marks.

- `e2e/editor/editor-status.spec.ts`: header cloud icons and keyboard tooltips, Saved on joining with nothing to store (Epo 2026-10-20), immediate Syncing during edits and checkpoint waits, Saved after acknowledgment, older receipts preserving newer pending edits, Offline retained through edits and late acknowledgments, reconnect resending pending checkpoints, and status removal in View mode. A note on screen whose reconnect is slowed by the open budget (the mock room's `setCollaborationSlowed`) keeps its editor, reads Reconnecting, and after 5 s holds the sync indicator's tooltip open with the slowed line, gone once the room syncs (Epo 2026-10-20; fails with the header's line or the editor's report reverted).

Seeded editor runs use `node_modules/.vite-editor-e2e` for Vite's dependency cache,
separate from a running developer server's cache. Vite prebundles the export
worker's `buffer` and `katex` dependencies so the first Word export cannot trigger
late dependency optimization and reload concurrent browser tests.
Editor benchmark readiness accepts Synced, Syncing and Saved; durability and
save-cycle measurements still wait specifically for Saved.

MSW workspace seed-count check: reload Workspaces; English Literature shows zero chapters and zero source files, while opening it still lists its Gatsby study note. Workspace totals are derived from seeded chapter and source-file records in src/mocks/db.ts.

Biology quiz visual check: with MSW enabled, open `/materials/qz_1?mode=edit` or either Biology note's quiz block. Verify 10 questions, all seven answer types, both layouts, formulas and the surface-area graph; open a question's Worked solution in its editor outline. Open `/quizzes/attempts/at_1` and expand marking schemes/worked solutions to inspect all six chart styles, calculation methods, tables and partial credit. The saved score is 13.5/21. Check desktop and phone widths, and save an edited question to verify the fixture remains valid quiz content.

Client export diagnostic: `node bench/editor/scripts/export-probe-server.mjs`, then `node bench/editor/scripts/export-probe.mjs`. A dedicated production bundle measures Markdown serialization and HTML-to-DOCX generation in the window and a module worker at normal and 4x CPU throttle, using 1,000/9,800 nodes and a 1.96 MB source case. Records elapsed time, interval delay and worker/image compatibility failures under ignored `bench/editor/.results/export-2026-09-27/`. This is a local conversion probe, not an end-to-end export or CI gate.

- `src/features/notes/export/export.test.ts`: readable feature-matrix export with its seeded image caption, seven answer types and multipart solutions, Markdown escaping/nesting, blue DOCX callouts and void dividers, unsupported/missing content, a Mermaid diagram the renderer refuses written into Word as its source in a code paragraph (Epo 2026-10-23), figure deduplication, native TOC placement, repeated/Unicode headings, exclusion of answer labels, and an interactive HTML block exported as an `Interactive snippet` link to the note with `block=<id>` in Markdown and DOCX without calling the figure renderer.
- `e2e/editor/exports.spec.ts`: actual toolbar Markdown (zipped with the seeded image) and DOCX downloads with resolved quiz/card content, native Word video metadata, TOC and page-reference fields, heading/label separation, TOC styles, update-on-open, hyperlinks/bookmarks, compatibility mode, embedded images and selected colors. Run `pnpm e2e:slow --config=e2e/editor/playwright.editor.config.ts e2e/editor/exports.spec.ts`.
- Client export implementation benchmark: set `EXPORT_CLIENT=1`, run `node bench/editor/scripts/export-probe-server.mjs`, then `node bench/editor/scripts/export-client.mjs`. Measures the production worker pipeline through returned blobs at document limits, 1,300 mixed blocks and 100 distinct formulas, including DOM figure rendering with 5,000 mounted paragraphs. Findings: `bench/editor/reports/2026-09-27-client-export-implementation.md`.
- [`e2e/editor/comments.spec.ts`](../e2e/editor/comments.spec.ts): Cursor-only and empty-block comments persist the containing block ID without text anchors; selected-text comments and a native selection made in the same task as the toolbar Comment click or as Ctrl+K (the command palette must store the range Slate has not synced yet) retain their quote, anchors and highlight. Setup verifies the selected text and empty-block deletion preserves the next paragraph; every case exposes the saved thread beside the block. A deleted block's thread lists with its quote in the toolbar's document comments next to a no-block thread (replies work there) and returns beside the block after Undo; at 360 px the document comments button and popover sit inside the screen.
- `e2e/editor/equations.spec.ts`: Block/inline opening and closing preserve geometry, block keyboard/menu buttons stack vertically while inline formulas have only a menu vertically centred on the field within 1 px, ATP text and math carets share a baseline, native physical arrow shortcuts work at text boundaries and survive commit while word interiors remain text, and mouse-drag selection keeps one MathLive instance with readable app-theme colors when system and app themes differ. Formula menus insert matrices/templates, switch modes, copy/paste LaTeX, and reopen after outside dismissal or removal of an editor with its menu open without browser errors. Committed matrix/template placeholders render as boxes and reopen as editable slots. A formula committed as `\cssId{capy-probe}{x}` previews the command as text and puts no such id into the page (security regression: read-only formulas draw MathLive's HTML commands as text). A click selects an inline or block formula without opening it, and Backspace or Delete then removes it; formulas open on a double click.
- `e2e/editor/formula-metrics.spec.ts`: Plain formula text retains its view/edit font and width; single/multiple-character conjugates use one arrow step per character in both directions and remain editable, while fraction navigation retains its native stops.
- `bench/editor/scripts/formula-parity.audit.ts` (`pnpm bench:formula`, not in CI; run it on MathLive upgrades, output in `bench/editor/.results/formula-parity/`): Checks all 13 MathLive Insert commands and 25 matrix sizes, empty/filled in inline/block modes (152 cases). Asserts view/edit dimensions and per-glyph/bar geometry within 0.1px, identical fonts/text, valid rendering and LaTeX round trips. Captures every pair and attaches geometry JSON. The original KaTeX comparison and MathLive follow-up are in `artifacts/2026-09-28-formula-parity/`.
- `e2e/editor/formula-opening.spec.ts`: Checks that an inline formula near the line end and its following text retain their positions/dimensions when editing opens, with a working overlay menu. Samples the first eight animation frames across five opening/closing cycles of a long, wrapped inline formula, alternating Enter and blur to commit; no frame may lose the formula text or collapse its width. Reproduces the cached-import opening flash and the empty preview frame on commit.
